Releasing
Session: ADB991-claude-20261123-b8a8

Not attempted in Lean this run (the sweep proved #5331 in the same file instead). Notes for the next person:

- The refutation needs three things the library does not provide in a ready form: (1) a product group `G = ℝ≥0ˣ × Multiplicative (ZMod 3)` with all the instances of the statement and an explicit `χ : PontryaginDual K → PontryaginDual G` extending characters of `K = ker m ≅ ZMod 3`; (2) the fact that `lcaFourier μ` of a function of left-isotype `ω` (i.e. `f(k⁻¹x) = ω(k) f(x)`) is supported on characters whose restriction to `K` is `ω⁻¹` (or `ω`, depending on the Fourier sign convention), so that for `ω ≠ ω⁻¹` the band condition over `χ ω` forces `lcaFourier μ (modulationWeight m b φ) = 0`, together with Fourier injectivity on Schwartz–Bruhat functions of `G` to conclude that the test itself is zero; (3) the action `A` of the remaining trivial-channel tests on the nontrivial isotypes. For (3), `A` is only known on compactly supported tests, so one needs density of `BruhatCompactSupport G` in `SchwartzBruhat G` plus continuity of `A`, or the explicit convolution of `existsUnique_schwartzBruhat_zeroLineAction` named in the docstring.
- With these, a vector `v(t, j) = h(log t) ζ^j` (`h` a smooth compact bump, `ζ = e^{2πi/3}`) is killed by every `A (φ n ω)`, so the identity is not in the strong closure.
- Check first whether the band convention in `modulatedFrequencyBand` makes the support condition `ω` or `ω⁻¹`; the argument needs the two to differ, which is why ℤ/3 is used rather than ℤ/2.
